criteria.criterion: Grep of .github/workflows/ci.yml: in each of the fmt, clippy and test jobs, an actions/cache/restore step for gitleaks and one for the athena binary come before the step named 'Set up (pinned toolchain, gitleaks, athena)'. Each key uses hashFiles over the files that decide the install. Every `uses:` line is still pinned by a 40-character SHA.
criteria.evidence: Restore order and pinning are met. The policy test every_job_restores_the_tool_caches_before_it_runs_the_setup_step passes, and workflow_actions_are_pinned in ci_shards.rs passes. A grep found all 44 `uses: actions/cache*` lines pinned to 5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684. The gitleaks key (athena.toml plus OS and arch) is right. The athena key is not over 'the files that decide the install': it hashes only 'crates/**/*.rs', 'crates/**/Cargo.toml', the xtask equivalents and five root files. The binary also embeds crates/athena-context/prompts/*.md (lib.rs:35-65), crates/athena-cap-change/prompts and crates/athena-cap-study/prompts (lib.rs:21-31) and docs/system-facts.md (briefs.rs:1230), none of which are in the key.

criteria.criterion: ci.yml has matching actions/cache/save steps for those two caches in the same jobs. Each carries the existing condition: not a pull request, ref equal to the default branch, and no exact cache hit. Neither cache is saved from any other event.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds 'Save the gitleaks cache' and 'Save the athena binary cache' to fmt, clippy and test. Each has the condition `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == format('refs/heads/{0}', github.event.repository.default_branch) && steps.cache-*.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'`, and test adds `matrix.shard == 0`. No other job saves either cache. The new policy test asserts the condition in all three check jobs.

criteria.criterion: The history, attribution and pr-head jobs that also run the setup step get the same restore step before it, or the diff states in a comment why they do not.
criteria.evidence: The diff adds both restore steps before 'Set up' in history, attribution and pr-head, each with a comment saying they only restore. SETUP_JOBS in policy.rs includes all six jobs, and the test passes.

criteria.criterion: With a cached gitleaks and athena binary present and matching, `./setup.sh --ci` skips both installs and prints that it skipped them. Without them it installs as before. Run `cargo test -p xtask`, which must include a test that exercises the skip and no-skip decisions.
criteria.evidence: These tests pass: a_cached_athena_is_skipped_only_when_present_and_matching (no binary, no stamp, a matching stamp, a different stamp), a_cached_gitleaks_is_skipped_only_when_it_reports_the_pinned_version, and the_inputs_digest_changes_with_a_source_and_ignores_other_files. findings.summary: The athena binary cache key and the skip digest leave out files that the binary compiles in, so CI can restore and use an out-of-date binary
findings.evidence: The key and input_files() keep only *.rs files, Cargo.toml files and five root files. The binary also embeds crates/athena-context/prompts/{contract,reader,producer,verifier,planner,critic}.md (crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs:35-65), crates/athena-cap-change/prompts/*.md, crates/athena-cap-study/prompts/*.md and docs/system-facts.md (crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs:1230), all through include_str!. A commit that changes only a prompt leaves the key and the stamp unchanged, so the cache hits and setup --ci skips the build. History, attribution and pr-head then run `athena check` with a binary not built from the commit under test. The ci.yml comment and the CHANGELOG say 'a stale binary is never restored', which is false. The repo already defines the build inputs: BUILD_PATHS = [crates/, xtask/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, setup.sh] in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs:20. Fix: hash 'crates/**' and 'xtask/**' plus rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, athena.toml, defaults.toml, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md in both the key and inputs_digest, ideally from one shared list.
findings.location: .github/workflows/ci.yml athena-bin keys (all 6 restore and 3 save steps); xtask/src/main.rs input_files

findings.summary: The ci.yml hashFiles list and the Rust input_files list are kept in step by hand and no test checks them
findings.evidence: The doc comment says 'The CI cache key in .github/workflows/ci.yml hashes the same set', but nothing enforces it. A policy test could compare the patterns in the athena-bin key with the input set. The defaults model asks for rules enforced by mechanism.

findings.summary: Only a --ci build writes the stamp, so a later non-CI build can leave an out-of-date stamp next to a new binary
findings.evidence: write_stamp runs only when flags.ci is set. On a developer machine, run setup --ci, change the sources, then run a plain setup: the binary is rebuilt but athena.inputs still holds the old digest. If the sources go back to the old state and setup --ci runs again, it skips the build and keeps a binary built from different sources. Writing the stamp on every build_and_adopt, or deleting it on a non-CI build, removes this. CI runners start fresh, so this does not affect CI.

findings.summary: A restored binary reports the source commit of the run that built it
findings.evidence: build_info() embeds ATHENA_BUILD_COMMIT and is passed into Athena (wiring.rs:140) and `athena --version`. The candidate states this in ci.yml and the CHANGELOG. The CI jobs only run read-only checks, so the effect looks small, but any CI output that names the build commit will show an older commit.

findings.summary: The skip path never runs build_and_adopt's dirty-tree refusal
findings.evidence: cached_athena returns early before the `dirty && !flags.allow_dirty` check in build_and_adopt. This is harmless on CI checkouts but changes behaviour for a local `setup --ci` on a dirty tree.

summary: The wiring is right but the athena binary cache key is wrong, so this fails. ci.yml now restores the gitleaks and athena-binary caches before 'Set up' in all six jobs that run it. fmt, clippy and test shard 0 save them, on the default branch only and not after an exact hit. Every cache step uses the existing pinned actions/cache SHA. `setup --ci` skips the athena build when a stamp file matches a digest of the inputs, and skips gitleaks when the pinned version is already there. The new policy test, and a negative test that removes or moves a restore step, both pass. The problem is the key and the digest: they cover only *.rs files, Cargo.toml files and five root files. The binary also compiles in other files through include_str!: the prompt files under crates/athena-context/prompts, crates/athena-cap-change/prompts and crates/athena-cap-study/prompts, plus docs/system-facts.md. The repo's own list of build inputs (BUILD_PATHS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs) is all of crates/ and xtask/, plus Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and setup.sh. So a change to a prompt file alone leaves the key and the stamp unchanged, and CI restores and uses an out-of-date binary. That contradicts the claim in the ci.yml comment and the CHANGELOG that a stale binary is never restored. The fix is small: hash crates/** and xtask/** (plus rust-toolchain.toml, the root files, setup.sh and docs/system-facts.md) in both the key and inputs_digest, and check the two lists against each other in a test. I did not run ./setup.sh --ci itself (it is not on my allowed command list and writes outside the working directory). The skip and no-skip decisions are covered by unit tests, and I read the printed messages in the diff.
